thread.title: Stock Market Update: S&P Flat Ahead of iPhone Unveiling

title: Stock Market Update: S&P Flat Ahead of iPhone Unveiling
text:
Strong: Industrials, Energy, Health Care, Consumer Staples, Telecom Services Weak: Financials, Technology Moving the Market
WSJ reports that the U.S. is proposing a new round of trade talks with China
Micron (MU) leads chipmakers solidly lower after being downgraded to 'Neutral' from 'Buy' at Goldman; top-weighted tech sector underperforms
Energy shares rally as crude prices extend Tuesday's gains; prices boosted by Hurricane Florence and the EIA's weekly inventory report S&P Flat Ahead of iPhone Unveiling 12-Sep-18 12:55 ET Dow +97.58 at 26068.64, Nasdaq -33.51 at 7938.99, S&P +0.02 at 2887.65
[BRIEFING.COM] The S&P 500 has struggled for direction following back-to-back victories on Monday and Tuesday, with the benchmark index flat at midday. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite and the small-cap Russell 2000 are underperforming, down around 0.5% apiece, but the Dow Jones Industrial Average is showing relative strength, up 0.4%.
The underperformance of the heavily-weighted information technology (-0.7%) and financials (-0.7%) sectors has kept the bulls in check, especially early when the S&P 500 was down as much as 0.3%. Within the tech space, chipmakers are particularly weak, evidenced by a 1.8% drop in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, with Micron (MU 41.42, -2.17) losing 5.0% following a downgrade at Goldman.
Headlines that the U.S. is proposing a new round of trade talks with China helped the market regain its footing though, pushing the S&P 500 to a new session high (+0.2%). Earlier in the week, it looked as if trade tensions between the U.S. and China might be tightening after Beijing told the WTO that it wanted to impose sanctions on Washington.
Meanwhile, Apple (AAPL 221.61, -2.24), the first U.S. company to hit a $1 trillion market cap, is down 1.0% ahead of today's annual product event, where the tech giant is expected to unveil its new iPhone lineup, including a new high-end iPhone that will likely be named the iPhone X Plus or the iPhone X Max.
Most of the S&P 500 sectors are in the green -- eight of eleven to be exact. Consumer staples (+1.3%) is being led by tobacco giants Philip Morris (PM 80.59,+ 3.14) and Altria (MO 63.76, +4.26), which are up 4.1% and 7.2%, respectively, after the FDA announced new steps to address the "epidemic" of youth e-cigarette use. The lightly-weighted telecom services space (+1.6%) is also notably strong.
Elsewhere, in the bond market, U.S. Treasuries have rebounded following yesterday's sell off, pushing the benchmark 10-yr yield, which hit a one-month high on Tuesday, lower by two basis points to 2.96%. The U.S. Dollar Index is down 0.2% at 94.88, and WTI crude futures are up 1.3% at $70.17/bbl.
Crude prices have been boosted by Hurricane Florence, which has continued barreling towards the East Coast, and the weekly EIA inventory report, which showed that U.S. crude stockpiles declined by 5.3 million barrels last week. The oil-sensitive energy sector is higher by 0.6%.
Reviewing today's economic data, which has been limited to the Producer Price Index for August and the weekly MBA Mortgage Applications Index thus far: Producer prices slipped 0.1% in August (Briefing.com consensus +0.2%), and core producer prices declined 0.1% (Briefing.com consensus +0.2%). Year-over-year, producer prices are up 2.8% (vs +3.3% in July) and core producer prices have risen 2.3% (vs +2.7% in July). The key takeaway from the report is that it will soothe some burgeoning inflation concerns, as the monthly declines led to a moderation in producer price inflation on a year-over-year basis. The latter point notwithstanding, the market is apt to maintain its view that the Federal Reserve remains on course to raise rates two more times this year. The weekly MBA Mortgage Applications Index decreased 1.8% to follow last week's downtick of 0.1%.
In addition, the Fed's Beige Book will be released at 2:00 PM ET. Add this to my Page Alerts . MARKET PLACE
